subject: SIG: follow-up - operational questions about KMS/HSM and key lifecycle
messages:
From: Julia Chen <julia.chen@acmepayments.com>
To: Ethan Park <ethan.park@redwood.com>
Cc: security@acmepayments.com
Date: Tue, 21 Nov 2028 09:02:00 -0800
Subject: SIG follow-up: clarifying encryption operations and KMS/HSM handling

Ethan,

Thanks again for the SIG responses you sent last week. The security team reviewed Section 4 (Encryption and Key Management) and had a few operational clarifications before we mark the section complete. We're primarily trying to validate day-to-day controls and evidence we can reference in our assessment. High-level asks below — short bullets are fine.

1) Key creation and escrow: who can create customer-facing KEKs/DEKs in Redwood-managed KMS? Is there an audit process for manual key creation?
2) HSM usage: do you use a cloud KMS HSM cluster (e.g., vendor-managed HSM) or a customer-dedicated HSM instance? Is the HSM FIPS level and which CSP's HSM?
3) Rotation cadence: documented default rotation cadence for long-lived KEKs and recommended rotation for DEKs used in production tokens (if different)? Any automated rotation policies?
4) Cross-region replication: when keys are replicated for failover, how are rotation and access controls synchronized across regions?
5) Evidence: we need a short ops summary and two sample artifacts (audit log extract showing key creation and a redacted rotation event). Can you provide these as attachments or point to a zipped evidence bundle?

We're on a fairly tight timeline for our internal SIG close — would like to get answers by EOD Thursday (Nov 23). Happy to hop on a 30-min call if easier.

Thanks,
Julia Chen
Senior InfoSec Analyst
Acme Payments

From: Ethan Park <ethan.park@redwood.com>
To: Julia Chen <julia.chen@acmepayments.com>
Cc: hannah.schmitt@redwood.com, marcus.lin@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 21 Nov 2028 11:14:23 -0800
Subject: Re: SIG follow-up: clarifying encryption operations and KMS/HSM handling

Julia —

Appreciate the clear list. I pulled Marcus (Security) and Hannah (Compliance) into thread and sketched answers below. Attached is an operational one-pager and an XLS with the completed SIG encryption fields (redacted where appropriate). If anything needs more detail we can either add an audit extract or schedule a short call.

Quick answers (summary):
1) Key creation/escrow: Redwood operates customer keys in a tenant-scoped KMS namespace. Key creation is performed by our control plane service; only the platform key-op service principal can create root KEKs. Platform engineers do not create customer KEKs manually except under documented emergency change and with JIRA approval and two-person review. All key creation events include an immutable audit entry.

2) HSM usage: For hosted mode customers we use cloud-provider managed HSM clusters (currently AWS CloudHSM for our us-region primary offering). For Dedicated and Private deployments customers can bring their own HSM or we deploy a dedicated HSM appliance in-customer VPC when contracted. All HSMs are FIPS 140-2 Level 3 validated by vendor certification; specific CSP and model details are captured in the attached ops summary.

3) Rotation cadence: Default KEK (customer root) rotation: every 24 months by policy; recommended DEK (data encryption keys used per-object/per-bucket) rotation: automatic rekeying on re-issuance or every 90 days depending on workload. Automated rotation is supported via scheduled key-rotation jobs; emergency rotations can be triggered with an audited runbook and require approval from two platform SREs.

4) Cross-region replication: Keys are replicated using asymmetrically-wrapped key material with replication only after successful KMS ACL checks. Rotation events are propagated via the control plane; we use versioned key metadata and a consensus check to ensure all replicas have the same active and previous key versions before cutover. Access controls are enforced by region-local IAM roles with central RBAC mapping.

5) Evidence: Attached: redwood_kms_hsm_operational_summary.pdf (ops description, HSM vendor/model, certs) and sig_completed_section_encryption.xlsx with our completed SIG cells. For audit excerpts we can provide a redacted log extract showing key creation and a rotation event. Let us know the preferred format (CSV/JSON) and redaction level.

If the team wants a short call, we're free Wed afternoon (Nov 22) 2–4pm PT.

ethan.park@redwood.com | +1 415-555-0192

Ethan, thanks — this is very helpful. A couple quick follow-ups from our security engineer:

- For the policy-driven KEK rotation (24 months) do you maintain previous key versions for decryption? How many previous versions are retained and is that retention configurable per customer?
- For DEK automated rekeying: is the rekey operation an online re-encryption or do you rely on lazy rewrap on access? Is there a risk window while rekeying occurs?
- For Dedicated/private HSM deployments: can you confirm whether HSM key material ever leaves the customer's VPC / appliance? If you offer managed HSM we need the exact wording we can put into the contract (e.g., "HSM key material is never exported in cleartext outside the FIPS module").

We would prefer the audit log excerpt in CSV and a redaction that removes customer IDs but preserves timestamps and event types. If you can provide that by EOD Wed that would keep us on schedule. Also Wed 2–4pm PT works; please send a calendar invite if you can.

Thanks,
Julia

From: Ethan Park <ethan.park@redwood.com>
To: Julia Chen <julia.chen@acmepayments.com>
Cc: hannah.schmitt@redwood.com, marcus.lin@redwood.com
Date: Wed, 22 Nov 2028 13:30:00 -0800
Subject: Re: SIG follow-up: clarifying encryption operations and KMS/HSM handling

Julia —

Responses inline below and I've attached the requested CSV audit excerpt (redacted_customer_audit_extract.csv).

- Previous key versions: we retain the last 3 key versions by default for KEKs (used for decryption and key rollover rollback) and that is configurable per-account with an allowable range 1–7. The retention applies to wrapped key metadata — master key material is not re-exposed.

- DEK rekeying: we support both online re-encryption (proactive background job) and lazy rewrap-on-access. For high-throughput workloads we recommend proactive background re-encryption to avoid a concentrated latency bump; the background process performs chunked rewrap with transactional checkpoints to limit risk window. The lazy method keeps a short risk window (access-time rewrap), and we log and monitor rewrap failure rates.

- HSM key material: for Dedicated/Private deployments where a customer-provisioned HSM/appliance is used, key material never leaves the HSM in cleartext — export is disabled by default and documented in the deployment runbook. For our hosted offering using CSP-managed HSM, we use a provider's FIPS-validated HSM and the modules do not export private key material in cleartext; exact contract language we propose: "HSM private key material is never exported in cleartext outside the FIPS module; any wrapping/unwrapping operations are performed inside the module." We can include the vendor certification references in the ops summary.

Attached: redacted_customer_audit_extract.csv, and I've updated the SIG spreadsheet with these clarifications. Landing action: Marcus will join Wed 2pm PT to walk through the audit extract and answer any technical follow-ups.

See you on the call — calendar invite sent.

Thanks,
Ethan
